title: Recall addition and subtraction facts to 20 using mental strategies (make ten, doubles)

lesson.title: Make Ten and Doubles: Fast Facts to Twenty

steps.say: You already know that adding ten to a number is super easy — ten plus three is thirteen, quick as a blink. So here is our secret: when a fact feels slow, we change it into a ten fact first.

visual.caption: Ten plus three lands on thirteen

steps.say: Let us try eight plus five. Eight is so close to ten — it only needs two more. So we break the five into two and three. First we give the two to the eight, and that makes a perfect ten.

visual.caption: Hop 2 from eight to make ten

steps.say: Now we still have three left over from that five. Ten plus three is thirteen. So eight plus five equals thirteen, and we never had to count on our fingers.

visual.caption: Second hop of 3: eight plus five is thirteen

steps.say: Here is our other helper: doubles. Doubles are the facts your brain already loves. Seven and seven, like seven hockey cards in each hand, is fourteen. When you spot a double, just say the answer — no strategy needed.

visual.caption: Two groups of seven make fourteen

steps.say: Now watch a mistake lots of kids make. Some say eight plus five is ten. They gave the two to the eight to make ten, then forgot the three that was left over. Do not lose that leftover piece! Five is two and three, so after you make ten you must always add the rest.

visual.caption: The 5 splits into 2 and 3 — keep the 3!

steps.say: So remember: slide over to make ten, then add what is left, and if you see a double, you already know it.

lesson.answer: Make ten first, then add the leftover — and if it is a double, you already know it.

practice.question: At the corner store in Kelowna you have nine dollars in your pocket, and your grandma gives you six more dollars. Use the make ten trick: how many dollars do you have now? Try drawing your own number line to show the two hops.
practice.answer: Fifteen dollars. Nine needs one more to make ten, so split the six into one and five. Nine plus one is ten, then ten plus five is fifteen.
